utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Madam Registrar, good morning to you. Could you call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is the case number IT-03-68-T, the Prosecutor versus Naser Oric.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Oric, can you follow the proceedings in your own language?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours, ladies and gentlemen. I can follow the proceedings in my mother tongue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. You may sit down. Good morning to you. Appearances for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. My name is Patricia Sellers with the Office of the Prosecutor, and with me are co-counsels Mr. Gramsci Di Fazio, Ms. Joanne Richardson, and our case manager, Ms. Donnica Henry-Frijlink, and good morning to the Defence team.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Good morning to you, Madam, and good morning also to the rest of the team. The appearances for Naser Oric.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours. My name is Ms. Vasvija Vidovic, and together with John Jones I appear on behalf of Naser Oric. With us are our legal assistant, Ms. Adisa Mehic, and our CaseMap manager, Mr. Geoff Roberts. Good mornings to the colleagues from the OTP.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Good morning, Madam Vidovic, to you and the rest of the team. Before we bring in the witness, a few housekeeping matters. I was looking at the schedule, our timetable, and I would like to update you on a few. First of all, we spoke yesterday of having the sittings of the week starting the 12th up to the 16th, that's next week, shifted to the morning with the exception of Monday, the 12th. I wish to confirm to you that it is being -- it has been changed as I suggested, in other words, 12th we will be sitting in the afternoon. The rest of that week we will be sitting in the morning. Then I also noticed later on that the last week of this month, the week starting 26th of September right through and including Friday, 30th September. Monday and Friday we were sitting in the morning in Courtroom I, while Tuesday, Wednesday, and Thursday we were supposed to sit in this courtroom in the afternoon. I know that we are going to have some Judges from somewhere visiting here, and they will probably be using this courtroom in the morning and that's probably why we are shifted in the afternoon. However, I think that we can still shift those three days, Tuesday, Wednesday, and Thursday, from the afternoon to the morning if we sit in Courtroom II. So please check whether that is possible. If it is possible, let's move to Courtroom II, unless I hear any objections to the contrary from the parties. Okay. Then we had spoken about the week in October when I had told you that we may have some problems and to which Madam Vidovic referred yesterday. That's the week starting on the 3rd of October right through the 7th, right through the 7th. The position is as follows: We will be sitting on plan the 3rd, the 4th, and the 5th, the 3rd, the 4th, and the 5th. But we will not be sitting at all on the 6th and on the 7th, because on those two days at least two of us are seriously hampered. All right? So that's the position for the time being. We are telling you this now so that you can prepare beforehand and schedule out -- spread out the witnesses accordingly. I have read the Prosecution response to the Defence motion filed under Rule 92 bis regarding Avdo Huseinovic. I need to discuss it with the other two Judges of course. We haven't had a chance to discuss it as yet. We will discuss it between today and tomorrow, and we will try to have a decision ready either end of this week or early next week. All right? Thank you. Any preliminaries? Prosecution? Defence?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Neither from the side of the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's bring the witness in and let's continue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Tiro.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Welcome back. I hope you had a good rest. Yesterday you testified for 3 hours and 15 minutes. Today I suppose the Defence will finish with your examination-in-chief and we will start with the cross-examination. So let's proceed. Please may I remind you that you are still testifying pursuant to the solemn declaration that you entered yesterday, namely to testify the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Examined by Ms. Vidovic: [Continued]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Tiro.

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yesterday when we interrupted our examination-in-chief, I was asking you about some events concerning your brother and about Mr. Stanisa Stevanovic. I will pursue this issue further.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the usher please give a document, an excerpt from Nijaz Masic's book to the witness. The book is called "Truth About Bratunac."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Tiro, I showed you this excerpt during proofing.

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please pay attention first to the author of the book whose name is Nijaz Masic, the book's title is "Truth About Bratunac," and we have a table with list of victims with the various columns, name and last name, father's name, year of birth, place of birth, date of death or date since the person is considered missing. Could you now take a look at the name which is the sixth on the list from the beginning of it. This is Tiro Mehmet, son of Alija, born in 1967 in Zapolje. The date is the 12th of April of 1993 when he was killed or disappeared, and the place where he disappeared is Srebrenica. I wanted to ask you the following: You told us you were born in Zapolje and that your father's name is Alija and your brother's Mehmet. Am I correct?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Apart from your brother, Mehmet Tiro, was there any other person called Mehmet Tiro, son of Alija in Zapolje?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is your family, the Tiro family, the only family in that area with that last name and do you originate from there?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: We are the only Tiro family in Zapolje because we moved from Visegrad, my father did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say "the only family" you mean the only Tiro family?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment. Yes, Madam Sellers.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, we're having a bit of difficulty just finding the name on the document --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It's on the second page. It's not on the first page. I had difficulties, too, but if you turn to the second page it's the sixth one from the top.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The sixth name on the second page then. I wanted to ask you the following: Was your brother born in 1967?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell the Chamber when he was born?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was born on the 25th of July, 1968.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it correct that he was killed or went missing in Srebrenica on the 12th of April of 1993?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you by the end of 1992 know of his fate?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did many people from your immediate surroundings know of his fate?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The author of the book, Mr. Nijaz Masic, did he consult anyone from your family ever to verify this piece of information?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could this document be assigned an exhibit number, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, by all means. And this will become Defence Exhibit 73 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: 733, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Tiro, I would kindly ask you to take a look at another document.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And I would ask the usher to put this document before the witness.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This is a list of soldiers who received salaries for August and half of September in Radijevici. The number is 04359987. Mr. Tiro, please go to the last of the three pages that were put before you. I will read it aloud for you. Did you find the last page? It is stated here, ends with number 95. The above-mentioned soldiers received their salaries for August and half of September. The Djoko Djokic unit of Fakovici, the date is the 25th of November, 1992, company commander, Vukoman Simic. Could you go back to the title of the document, Mr. Tiro. It is stated here: "List of soldiers who received salaries for August and half of September in Radijevici." Could you tell the Trial Chamber the following: The village of Radijevici, is it actually a hamlet of another village?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is one of the hamlets around Fakovici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, please go to number 51 and take a look at that name, Stanisa Stevanovic. Can you see it?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I wanted to ask you the following: In the area of Fakovici, was there any other Stanisa Stevanovic, apart from the one that you mentioned?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know the area well?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is my immediate environment, the immediate area where I lived. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, could we assign the number to this document, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. This will become, Madam Vidovic, Defence Exhibit D734.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I want to ask you something else about Mr. Stanisa Stevanovic. Do you know if he had any children?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Seven.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us whether these were boys or girls?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Six girls and one boy.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Which one of them was his youngest?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: His son was the youngest.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I don't know whether you have already been given a new document, but in that case I would kindly ask the usher to put it before the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Is there relevance why we should know how many children he had?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. It is not the number of children that is important but rather this document where it is mentioned what the money was that was paid out to his children because he was a fighter; that is relevant concerning Mr. Stevanovic's evidence. At that time he claimed something that was quite different from what is in the documents and you will realise it from the next document.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Tiro, please take a look at this document with a title "TO Skelani." The date is the 29th of October of 1992, list of fighters of the Djoko Djokic unit in Fakovici who received monetary allowance for children, pupils. Please take a look at 11. The name is Stanisa Stevanovic (Stojka), under that Dragoljub. Between these two names, do you recognise the names of Mr. Stanisa Stevanovic's children?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. These are the two of the youngest ones.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And is that the person that you mentioned throughout your evidence?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, could we assign an exhibit number to this document, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, this will be D735.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: The youngest of the two, Judge Eser would like to know who the youngest of the two were, whether it's Stoja or Dragoljub.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: One of the Judges would like to know who was the younger of the two children mentioned here.

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Dragoljub.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And thank you, Mr. Tiro, for the clarification.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, might I just ask one other clarification matter. Madam Vidovic has asked a question about: And is the person, I'm at 9609, and is that the person you mentioned throughout your evidence. Just to clarify, she's not referring to either of the two people mentioned in the document. Is she referring back to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Stanisa Stevanovic --

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: It's unclear from the transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yeah, okay. I thank you, but I think it's clear enough. Let's proceed. I think we are satisfied.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Tiro, concerning this I would like to ask you the following: If one was to claim that Mr. Stevanovic, Stanisa, on the 25th of August of 1992 was not in Bosnia but rather in Serbia, would that be correct?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. After you returned, after the incident when your brother-in-law was killed, did you immediately discuss it with the people around you and did you learn something about where at that time Stanisa resided?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us what it is that you finally found out?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: A certain Saban of Zanjevo told me that Stanisa, right after Bradjevina fell, moved into his house in Zanjevo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you have any knowledge until when Stanisa Stevanovic lived in that Muslim's house?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Until 2003.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it true that he refused to move out of the house after the end of the war?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he wouldn't move out.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Another question concerning that. Mr. Tiro, after the fall of Srebrenica and after you've reached the free territories, did you give any statements, either you or any member of your family, about the incident that you've described for the Chamber concerning your brother-in-law? Did you give any statements to the authorities in Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I gave those statements in Zivinice.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: To whom?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: A person from Sarajevo came. He said he worked for the Tribunal in The Hague, for the Prosecutor's office. And I gave statements concerning my wounding and the killing of my brother-in-law and the disappearance of my brother.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Another question concerning this topic: Did Stanisa Stevanovic after the incident try to establish some contact with you?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, on two occasions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you explain, please?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: He tried to greet me in order to talk about my brother-in-law.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you accept his -- this conversation?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, and I never will.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us what was the last time he tried?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Two months ago in front of the municipality building in Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. I will now move on to a different topic. Mr. Tiro, do you remember where you were on the 5th of October of 1992?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What were you doing there?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was working. I was helping people to provide some shelter. I'm a construction worker otherwise, and I loved helping whoever so that people would have a place to stay.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did I understand correctly that you were working in construction, that you were repairing houses?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We tried to improve the situation with the houses so that people could find shelter.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Did you move towards Fakovici in that period?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: My relatives came in the evening, and they told me that an operation will take place there for liberation and that we should go there to look for food.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When did you set out?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Around 10.00 p.m. We travelled the whole night to get there to find some food.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Those relatives of yours, who were they? Civilians or were they armed?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Civilians.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was this a dangerous trip for you to Fakovici?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not dangerous but very dangerous.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: That entire area joins the Drina Valley, so you didn't really know which direction you could be struck from by a shell or a bullet or something.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The direction that you were going in towards Fakovici, were there any particularly dangerous places there?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Which ones?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was dangerous to pass Spat, Zalazje. Zalazje was mined and Spat -- the Serb army was stationed at Spat.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Nevertheless, did you manage to get close to Fakovici?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How far did you get?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: To the outlying areas of Fakovici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did I understand you properly, that you arrived there on the 6th of October, 1992?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you manage to actually enter Fakovici?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please explain to the Trial Chamber why not?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: You could not enter Fakovici itself because there was shelling and also heavy artillery fire from Radijevici and Boljevici as well as from across the Drina, from Serbia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And which direction did you come from to get to Fakovici?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I came with my cousins from the direction of Grabovacka Rijeka.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you manage to enter some of the outlying houses there?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I entered one house. I found some wheat. I didn't have time for anything else and then I went back.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At the time when you were there you spent a certain amount of time there. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you able to see any part of Fakovici?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The direction from Grabovacka Rijeka -- actually, from that direction you can see all of Fakovici, especially up to the centre, the first part of Fakovici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what did you see on the 6th of October, 1992? Did you see burned buildings within Fakovici itself?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I just want to ask you something else. Did you go there just with your cousins or were there any other people there on that day, on the 6th of October?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was civilians there, nobody could prevent them. They had to go and look for food. There were too many of them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many of them were there?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it was in the thousands. There were thousands of people going there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. When you returned to your own village, did you talk to anyone who was in Fakovici the day before?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: With whom?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: With my cousin, Safet Memic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Safet Memic, did he belong to a certain armed group of fighters?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he himself have a weapon?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did he get the weapon from?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: He found a rifle near Bradjevina in the forest.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he hand the rifle over to somebody? Did anybody ask him to hand over that rifle?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, he did not hand it over, even though they did ask for it. But he needed the rifle for his own needs in order to go and look for food.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did I understand you properly that he simply did not give up this rifle?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right, no, he didn't give it up.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At the time was he under anyone's command?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I would like to go back to the conversation you said you had with him. What did he tell you about the events of the 5th of October in Fakovici? If he said anything to you, what did he say?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember that well. He said that there were a lot of our people that had been killed in Fakovici, that they had captured weapons, ammunition, a large quantity of that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Could you please tell me if he told you how those people were killed in Fakovici, our people, what you described as our people?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Our people were killed by shells, mines, from machine-gun nests, from the houses. Everybody was in their own houses. They were all particularly up on the first floor of the houses so that they could have a better view of where our people were coming from.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did he personally tell you that --

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, it seems to me that the witness there is speculating as to why people might have been anywhere that he claims that there were placed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] With what authority do you maintain what you've just stated, that our -- your people were killed by shells, mines, from machine-gun nests, from the houses. Everyone was in their own houses. They were all particularly up on the first floor of the houses? Is this what you were told or is this what you think happened or you believe happened?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. My own cousin told me this, Your Honours, and he was there.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Talking about the houses and this shooting from the houses and the casualties within Fakovici, could you tell us exactly what he told you?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: He exactly told us that they were hit by sniper -- by machine-gun fire from the houses, even from the school. They were fired upon from various weapons, and they didn't even manage to bring out a certain number of our people from Fakovici, that their dead bodies remained in Fakovici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Tiro, according to what you know, were there many casualties and killed and wounded amongst the Muslim civilians on that day?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know the number, but there were many of them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On that day, on the 6th of October, 1992, did you see any of those people who were wounded or killed?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Those who were on the outskirts of Fakovici near to where I was. I did see them but not in Fakovici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm asking you about what you saw.

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many of those people did you see?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I perhaps saw about ten people who were wounded, not wounded by bullets, mind you, but by shelling.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. You mentioned that your cousin also talked to you about arms that were seized?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember exactly what he said?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember that he said that they had captured a large quantity of light and heavy weapons as well as two tractors of ammunition.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Now I would like to ask you something else. I would like to move to Bjelovac. Mr. Tiro, you said that you spent the fall and winter of 1992 in Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the situation in Srebrenica deteriorate as time passed from October onwards?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: The situation was getting worse.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember whether you went on a food expedition sometime in mid-December 1992?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember when this was?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 14th or the 15th, either of those two dates.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Why did you decide to go there?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: We decided because there was a food crisis and I had to go.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But how did you find out that you were supposed to go to Bjelovac?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: A friend of mine, Bego Begic from Biljaca, told me that they were going to go to liberate that area because there was a large quantity of food there. That's an area with a lot of fields.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Bego Begic, is he a civilian or was he an armed person at that time or was he a member of a unit, in other words?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. He was an elderly man. There was no question of him being a fighter. He could hardly walk.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. And what did you do?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I decided to go, and my cousins came by Suret and Enes Memic, and they had their houses on the outskirts of Bjelovac, so we set off for Bjelovac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where did you go?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: We left from Srebrenica through the forest. We reached Tri Kralja and then we could go no further.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please explain to the Trial Chamber what Tri Kralja is?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Tri Kralja are old mines of the Sase mines, the first old pits of the Sase mines.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you see Bjelovac from there?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It's at an elevation that provides a good view of Bjelovac and Zalazje.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you go there by yourself?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. There were thousands of people besides me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You explained to us that you set off by yourself with your cousins, but what happened then? What was this like?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was no need to tell anyone anything or it was enough to see a person put a rucksack on their back and set off and then people would start to go behind you because it was evident that people were then going somewhere to get food.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say a "rucksack" is that a military bag or is that a bag that you used to put food in?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's a large bag that you put on your back where you put your food in, and that was a kind of code word for the civilians.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. On that occasion, according to what you know, did the fighters organise you in any way to go into action, you, your cousins, and the people that you knew around you?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. The fighters would never organise or call us to do something like that or lead us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Tiro, can you tell the Trial Chamber why the fighters would not call you to come?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because we would reveal their positions and because there would be many casualties amongst the civilians, and that is why those people didn't want to get into -- get themselves into trouble.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, I -- you are assuming that about the fighters but I will ask you again. In relation to this action, did you have any - you and the people around you - did you have any information that any fighter had called any of those people and organised them to go into an action?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the way to Tri Kralja, did anyone stop you or not or possibly prevent you from continuing on your way?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. They were preventing us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please explain to the Trial Chamber who that was?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was a group of people who were armed. They were not Serbs, they were Muslims. They were standing on the road. They didn't allow us to pass. So we had to find another way, take a detour through the forest and then get to the top of Tri Kralja.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you or anyone else recognise anyone from that group?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I didn't recognise anyone. I just heard when we called out to one of them, I don't know what his last name, but they called him Soson.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what was this Soson doing?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Soson was shouting at us and turning us back. Don't go. Can't you see that there is shelling? You will all get killed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. How many people were in that group with you at the time?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was not possible to count them. There was always more than a thousand people, a thousand or more people.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did I understand you properly that you withdrew to Tri Kralja, deeper towards Tri Kralja?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We went to the top of -- the peak of Tri Kralja where the old pits were.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In relation to other people, this group around you where you were, did you have any advantage compared to other groups or other people around you?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We had the advantage that we -- that set us apart. There was an elderly man there, a hunter from Srebrenica, and he had binoculars with him and he was following the action and the fighting as it was unfolding.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And why was this -- these -- why were these binoculars useful for you? Were you interested in the action or were you interested in something else?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were only interested in seeing which part we could enter so we could get some food.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And please, could you tell the Trial Chamber, did you manage to go into Bjelovac on that day?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because of the dangerous shelling, the air force, the fighting.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say "the air force," what does that mean for you? Did you see something on the occasion?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We kept seeing two airplanes. They were going in the direction of Loznicka Rijeka along the asphalt road and they were bombing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You told us that you are familiar with the Bjelovac area, that you went to school there. Do you remember which parts of Bjelovac were shelled? Were they flying over the entire area?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were mostly going towards Loznicka Rijeka and Sikiric. That Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. is where they bombed the most.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That area where you were, Tri Kralja, were you able to see Kunjerac?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Kunjerac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you able to see it well?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Kunjerac was visible because this is thousands of metres above Kunjerac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You're talking about Tri Kralja?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At the time could you hear shooting and see where it was coming from?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: The shooting itself was coming both from inside Bjelovac, from Sikiric and Loznicka Rijeka, but Kostanovici was the most dangerous place.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, just one correction, Your Honours. The witness said that Kunjerac was visible because it is about a thousand metres and above Kunjerac, and here it seems -- in the transcript it says a thousand metres above Kunjerac. Perhaps the witness can confirm what we said, that it is at an altitude of a thousand metres and is above Kunjerac.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, about a thousand metres.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Then I asked you how much time did you spend at Tri Kralja?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Almost three days.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. At any point did you manage to get into a part of Bjelovac?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Through Sase, the Muslim part of Sase, and Vlasovac we entered Kunjerac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many of you came to that area?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Almost a thousand of us entered. I really couldn't count because people were trampling over each other to get to the food.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you notice anything on the road towards Kunjerac as you were getting close to Kunjerac?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did you notice?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I was approaching Kunjerac and going into the house of Ivan Stojanovic, because I knew him very well, I saw an anti-aircraft machine-gun and also a dead body next to it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just one moment, please. Mr. Tiro, what is a PAM?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is an anti-aircraft machine-gun.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Did you notice anything else?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I noticed some other bodies further away.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Just one moment. When you saw this PAM and you mentioned this body, did you look at the body?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. I looked at the body.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you recognise the person or not?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And whose body was it, could you please tell the Trial Chamber?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was Mitar, the photographer, I know him very well because I always went to him when I needed to have photographs for documents and everything.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where is this man from?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: From Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you mentioned that you saw more bodies around. Mitar and these dead people, were they Serbs?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Serbs.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What were they wearing?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mitar and a number of them were wearing multi-coloured camouflage uniforms.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would now like the usher to show the witness Defence Exhibit D49 -- D45, I apologise. 45. D45, D45. It's a large document. It's the list of killed fighters of the Bratunac Brigade. If it's easier, perhaps I can give my copy to the witness.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Tiro, could you please find the page beginning with the number 495.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, that number is on page 15. Both in the Bosnian and English versions, it's on page 15.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Tiro, could you please look whether you have in front of you the page that starts with the number 495?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please look at the name under 513?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It says here Ostoja Savic, son of Mitar [as interpreted], from Bratunac, killed on the 14th of December, 1992, the village of Kunjerac.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just one correction for the transcript. Savic Mitar, son of Ostoja, and not as it was stated earlier in the transcript. So it is Savic, Mitar, son of Ostoja. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Tiro, did you -- was this the person that you knew? Is this the name of the person whose body you found?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that his last name? Did you know him?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That is his last name and his father's name.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. You also told us that you saw some more bodies of people who were killed?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you said that some of them were wearing camouflage uniforms. Were they all wearing camouflage uniforms or were these other people wearing something else?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not all of them had camouflage uniforms. Some were wearing black uniforms with markings of the military police around their left arm.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You can take this document from the witness.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you still go to Vodovod?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because Vodovod was mined, and they told us that were some Red Berets there and we were frightened of them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. According to what you saw when you were still at Tri Kralja, was there major fighting going on in and around Bjelovac at the time?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From that place where you were, were you able to see anything burning in Bjelovac?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Bjelovac is below the hill, towards the Drina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And could you see the area of Loznicka Rijeka?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I could just notice -- when a plane was flying overhead and bombing, then I could see smoke. Otherwise, you couldn't see anything burning, house or anything like that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If I understood you properly, from that position you said earlier that you were able to observe the fighting. Did I understand you properly that you were able to look at the area of Kunjerac but not this other part of Bjelovac?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. As far as this other part of Bjelovac was concerned, you could only hear strong detonations and firing but nothing else.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What exactly could you see of Bjelovac, to avoid any confusion?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Only Kunjerac and a part of the entrance to Bjelovac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You note -- you said that you had noticed smoke from up above. Where was this coming -- smoke coming from, what was your impression?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: As soon as one of the two planes flew over, after it passed then you could see smoke. I couldn't tell whether it was a Serb or a Muslim house that was burning. I didn't see that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you very much. In the house that you entered, that you mentioned before, did you find anything there?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I found flour, plum brandy, rakija, and five kilogrammes of honey.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. And did you stay there for a while or did you move on?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. As soon as I took those things, I went back.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And which direction did you take?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: We took the direction below Vlasovac towards Gradina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And was this the area of Sase, as well as Gradina part of Sase?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Moving towards Sase, did you see anything else specifically?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did you see?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw an abandoned mortar and bodies next to it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where exactly did you see it?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just below the village of Vlasovac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you approach those people?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was good luck for us to see them first --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: It wasn't the bodies but the people.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And we saw them when we were still 50 to 60 metres away.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you recognise any of those people?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I recognised Ivko from Bjelovac and his son. They were standing next to the mortar.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember their last names?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe they -- their family name is Ilic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. You said, if I understood correctly, they stood next to the mortar. Who stood next to it?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Ivko was next to the mortar and his son was a bit further away and he held an automatic rifle in his hands.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you recall what sort of uniforms they wore?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Multi-coloured camouflage uniforms.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Tiro, Judge Eser asked you about the term of "neighbourhood" yesterday and how come you knew and had so many neighbours. Could you explain to the Chamber in our villages, in our part of the world, do people know each other, and is it a regular thing that they have extensive contacts with the people that are immediately next to them and in their environment?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: My neighbour is the person who lives in the village with me and also a person living five kilometres away.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I mentioned these people from Bjelovac. How did you know them, or rather why did you know people from Bjelovac?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know Bjelovac because I attended school there and I know Ivko. He used to drive the bus between -- rather, the bus of the Srebrenica Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. Express Company.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could I kindly ask the usher to put D507 before the witness. D507.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This is a list of military personnel of the Bratunac TO. Please turn to the page that says 3rd Company at the beginning. The number is 01315661. Can you see it, Mr. Tiro?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please take a look at numbers 5 and 6. Number 5, Ilic, Ivko, Dragan. And number 6, Ilic, Vase, Ivko of Bjelovac. Turn to the next page, please. As I explained yesterday, this should be a composite part of the previous page as well. Please take a look at the sixth -- at number 6 in the first column. Does it say "artillery"? Does this tally with what you saw that day when it comes to Mr. Ivko?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I was just being told that this has been given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Tiro, to continue. If I understood you correctly, you went towards Sase after that. Is it correct that there is a mine there?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you reach the mine?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you enter the mine on that day, either immediately or after a while? What was happening?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Perhaps after half an hour there was shelling again and it was the safest place to be and quite a number of us entered the mine because it was put in concrete, so it was quite solid.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If I understood correctly, there was shelling and that a large number of people entered the mine?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you familiar with the mine?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why were you familiar with it?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I got employed with the Majdenpek company that dealt with the mines, I worked in the field. I wasn't working only in the company headquarters, but all over the former Yugoslavia. I worked in Sase, in Loznica, Zajecar, and in Uzice.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say in Sase, did it have anything to do with the mine itself?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That was my first mission.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How much time did you spend there?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you were very familiar with the mine?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If I understood you correctly you spent two or three days there. Were you able to be there or could it have been possible for you to be there on the 17th of December?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, in the evening.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As of the moment when you entered together with those people, was the mine damaged? Could you explain it to the Chamber.

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is nothing to be damaged in the mine. It was the question of life or death for us and we had to take whatever we could get. We were not thinking of whether the mine would hold; we were sure it would.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But what was of specific interest for you in the mine?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that this is where the salt storage was used to put on roads when it was very cold, and we needed that salt for our food.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did I understand you correctly that the salt was used for roads in winter?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, in winter.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How did you know that?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because I used to work there and I know what they used it for.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Did you take some of the salt then?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell the Chamber, were you able to leave the mine on that day, or rather that evening, because you said that's when you arrived? This group of people, were you able to leave?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us why?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because of heavy shelling and shots being fired from heavy weapons.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you remain there throughout the night and how long did you stay there?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Until next morning, on the 18th.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you left the mine, what was the next thing that happened to you?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: The same again, shelling, air strikes, and a truck was hit at that moment. That's when my sister-in-law's sister was killed and her relative. There were quite a few wounded with them as well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Tiro, you attended school in that area and you were quite familiar with it. Were you able to assess where the shelling was coming from?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The shelling and the shots came from Bjelovac and Loznicka Rijeka up to Voljevica and from Serbia proper.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Madam Sellers.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: I imagine that the witness's testimony response to the question is shelling might have been coming from a certain direction, unless he's clarifying it, not from a place. There has been no testimony indicating that he would know that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Tiro, you've heard what Madam Sellers has just remarked. When you say that the shelling was coming from Bjelovac, Loznicka Rijeka, Voljevica, and from Serbia proper, do you mean to say that it was coming from those directions?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I want to ask you something else now. Do you recall if you had any knowledge then about Kostanovici, Vezovici, Neskovici?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was the strongest Serb stronghold and that's where there was strongest resistance and shooting.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On that day or generally speaking?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: On that day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why do you say that?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because I was unable to go through Kostanovici and Neskovici but rather I went through Vlasovac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Given that you were trying to go back to Srebrenica, was it easier to go through Neskovici, Vezovici, and Kostanovici, provided there was no shooting, and was it easier than the other route you took?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course, because there was an asphalt road there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And if I understood correctly, you couldn't use it because of the shooting. You couldn't go towards Vezovici and Kostanovici?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: To ask you something about a different thing: Were there any killed in your group because of that shooting?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there were killed and a number of wounded.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you take those people with you or were you simply running away?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was no time to get -- pull anyone out. We were saving our lives.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would kindly ask the witness to take a look at another document, please. This is a document coming from the Drina Corps command. The date is the 19th of December of 1992 sent to the General Staff of the VRS, signed by someone for Commander Colonel Milenko Zivanovic. This is a combat report.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Tiro, I would kindly ask you to direct your attention to item 2. Please take a closer look. It is stated here: "Our forces, during the 18th and 19th of December, 1992, they stabilised their defence in the area of responsibility of the Bratunac Brigade (according to the reconnaissance group report from the attack platoon the Sase mine is whole and undamaged.) A truck was destroyed via artillery fire as well as two motorised vehicles. Aviation destroyed the department store, the building of the municipality of the court, Crni Guber spa, and a part of the settlement in the villages of Pirici and Podloznik as well as some personnel losses." Did you understand this item, Mr. Tiro?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This document, this report, is dated December 19, 1992. First of all, Mr. Tiro, could you see here that it says that people from the assault platoon reported that the Sase platoon was undamaged? Is that what you were able to observe on the 18th of December of 1992?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, to clarify something in the transcript. I read out "according to the report of the reconnaissance group from the assault platoon or detachment."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Sase platoon, it should be the Sase mine, no?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Assault detachment but not from Sase, but it was learned from the assault detachment that the Sase mine was undamaged. Your Honour, this is a very important document for us and I will read it aloud again because the interpretation is incorrect.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Tiro, I will read it again. "Our forces, during the 18th and the 19th of December of 1992, stabilised their defence in the area of responsibility of the Bratunac Brigade (according to the report of the reconnaissance group from the assault detachment, the Sase mine is undamaged and whole)." Perhaps we shouldn't continue reading, it is not necessary, but rather I will reiterate the question. What you were able to observe on the 18th of December is what you described. Does that tally with what is stated in this document, that the Sase mine at that time was undamaged?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. To continue, it says here that the planes managed to destroy a truck.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment. It may say so in the Serbo-Croat version, I haven't checked it, but in the English translation it doesn't mention any planes destroying the truck. It says: "A truck was destroyed by artillery fire as well as two motorised vehicles." And then where the aviation comes in is in the next part. "Aviation destroyed the department store, municipality court, Crni Gruba spa and a part of the settlement in Srebrenica and made damage in the villages of Pirici and Podluznik." If the translation is not correct, please let us know.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I can't remember mentioning a plane. I mentioned artillery. I will reiterate the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Look at line 12, it says: "Thank you, to continue." It says here that the planes managed to destroy a truck. This is what we got. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will reiterate and it pertained to artillery.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did artillery shell a truck on that day? Did you see that on the 18th of December, 1992?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that the truck you mentioned a minute ago when a cousin of yours was killed?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us her name?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Adila Huremovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The document further states: "On the 18th and the 19th of December, 1992, they managed to stabilise their defence line in the area of responsibility of the Bratunac Brigade," and then the Sase mine is mentioned. Concerning that I want to ask you the following: You told us that you were there in that area in the evening of the 18th. Did you get an impression that the Serbs regained control, or rather was it your personal impression that the Serbs regained control of that area?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, because it was of importance for them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Tiro, leaving aside whether it was important for them, the mine, I wanted to ask you the following: Was it your personal impression that the Serbs gained control of that territory again?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please describe how you left the area?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But before that, Your Honour, could we assign an exhibit number to this document?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. This will become Defence Exhibit D736. And before we leave it Judge Eser would like to put a question to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: Just for a matter of clarification, since the Defence told us that there is some relevance where the truck was destroyed, now in this second paragraph we read that a truck was destroyed of artillery fire later on and it speaks of Srebrenica and so on. Now, the document is such, at least it does not appear quite clear where the truck was destroyed, whether it was in Sase or in Srebrenica, because Sase is mentioned in brackets and Srebrenica again. Of course I don't know whether it's relevant, but since you told us it might be relevant it would be good to clarify this point.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. It is important.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Tiro, could you tell us where the truck was destroyed and whether you saw it?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The truck was destroyed at the entrance towards Gradina called Kolonija.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it a part of Sase?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, a residential area of Sase where the workers of the mine lived.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Judge Eser.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: A further question. Were you also able to notice that in the document there is a mention of significant damage in the Muslim villages of Pirici and Podloznik?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard about it but I wasn't present.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On to a further topic, Mr. Tiro. If one was to claim that on the 18th of December of 1992 he or she was transported in a vehicle, in a Mercedes vehicle, from Podloznik, across Bjelovac, Biljaca, Zalazje to finally reach Srebrenica, would that be correct?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I want to know this first and foremost: Is it possible that a Mercedes vehicle or any other vehicle could move from Podloznik to Bjelovac before the war, during the war, and even nowadays?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And, Your Honours, could we be given the map that the witness was using yesterday, D727, in order for the witness to show us where Podloznik is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Tiro, before you point to Podloznik, just another question concerning Pirici. Are they in close proximity or not of Sikiric?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How close?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: About one kilometre away.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you please take a look at the map. Could you show where Sikiric is and then Pirici underneath, if you are able to find it. Pirici. Can you find Sikiric? That's close to Bjelovac.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You need to go further down, Mr. Tiro, further down the Drina. There -- that's Bjelovac. That's Loznicka and --

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sikiric and Pirici.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: He has circled --

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And Podloznik.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise, Your Honour. Perhaps this would be a good moment for a break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And I will continue later. I don't have too many questions left.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. We will have a 25-minute break. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I just want to make one brief announcement I already discussed with co-counsel -- I'm sorry, Defence counsel this morning, is that the Prosecution would have no new exhibits with this witness today. We might offer some exhibits, and we'll contact both your offices and the Defence this afternoon. At this moment we intend at the very most only to use exhibits that the Defence has already brought forward.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. How long do you anticipate your cross will take?

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'll take part of -- I'll take part of today and certainly a part of tomorrow. I might not use the entire time period we have today nor the entire time period of tomorrow though.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Will you be starting with the next witness tomorrow?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour. That is a very complex witness and the evidence will take a significant amount of time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I spoke with Mrs. Sellers about that and I kindly asked her to forward the documents that they intend to use in a timely fashion, the documents they intend to use in their cross-examination so that we could prepare for the re-direct because we were fair enough to do that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Let's have a 25-minute break then. Thank you. Or we can even make it 30 minutes. 30 minutes from now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So let's continue, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Tiro, we stopped as you were showing us Podloznik on the map. And before then you said that from Podloznik through Bjelovac to Srebrenica it wasn't possible to take that road by a vehicle. Could you please explain to the Trial Chamber why it was not possible for traffic to move from Bjelovac to Podloznik before the war and during the war in the course of 1992, 1993, and so on?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: The road from Podloznik through Loznicka Rijeka and Bjelovac towards Sase and Srebrenica -- actually, first of all, Podloznik didn't actually have a road, a proper road, that a vehicle could drive along.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just one moment, Mr. Tiro. Could you explain to the Trial Chamber how long is the asphalt road from Bjelovac towards Podloznik? Where does it stop, if it stops?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: The asphalt road from Bjelovac to Loznicka Rijeka and then it continues on towards Fakovici. From Loznicka Rijeka towards Podloznik there is four kilometres but that's not part of the road. That village actually didn't have a proper road.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So how could the population of Podloznik get to Loznicka Rijeka, Bjelovac, and so on?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: The inhabitants of Podloznik could go by horse or they could walk down to Loznicka Rijeka.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In other words, in 1992 the road from Podloznik to Bjelovac was not there?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Actually, that road is being cut through now, the road is being laid down now. I am in the committee overseeing that work.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Talking about the road -- now we're talking about the period of 18th of December, 1992, when you were there. Regarding the road of Bjelovac via Biljaca, could you please look at the map. Could you show the Trial Chamber where this asphalt road from Bjelovac to Srebrenica went.

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Bjelovac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you show that to the Chamber?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Biljaca, Kostanovici, Sase. You also have this over Kostanovici and then it comes to Sase and then it goes towards Srebrenica from Sase.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now I am going to ask you this: On the 18th, when you said that firing was coming from that direction, please, could you tell the Chamber these places that you indicated, Neskovici, Kostanovici, Obadi, and particularly Neskovici and Kostanovici, were these Serb areas?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: 100 per cent Serb areas.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And on that day, on the 18th of December, 1992, is it true that you could not take that direction towards Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because of their strongholds and because of the shootings.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The firing -- the fighting that was going on on that day?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Please, which road did you use that day? How did you return to Srebrenica? Could you please tell the Trial Chamber and maybe even show it to the Chamber on the map?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please show it on the map?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: We went over -- through Lasovac, Neskovici, Bjelovac, and then we bypassed here below to Vlasovac and that's how we came to Sase -- actually, Gradina and Sase. That pit is at Gradina where we hid. So that was the road. Kunjerac is somewhere around here and that's where we cut through.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How did you get to Srebrenica? Which direction did you take?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: From Gradina, from this pit, we went towards Lisac. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you show Lisac to the Trial Chamber and underline it, please.

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. And then go on?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: From Lisac we went to Tri Kralja, here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: And from Tri Kralja we came down towards Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Throughout the war do you know, do you personally know if at any time during the war the Muslims used this road, Bjelovac, Biljaca, Neskovici, and Kostanovici, and so on?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: During the war?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Asphalt road?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. It was not possible to use the asphalt road.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And why?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
