utterances.text: Because of their lines and strongholds and the firing from their side.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Which road did the Muslims use during the war in order to reach Srebrenica, if they were going in this area?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: All of these people who used the road were able to go from Mocevici towards Thorazac [phoen] and then from Podloznik towards Predola and then Storesk and then further up.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you indicate that on the map, please?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Lokve is here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please adjust the map so that we can follow. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Fetinici, Pljevlja, then Dimnici is here, and then we would go around Skenderici on the other side.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm asking you when you go towards Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that when we go towards Srebrenica, here between Spat we would pass directly towards Srebrenica through the forest.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Through the forest. Okay. Very well.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We no longer need the map. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now I would like to ask you something else. Do you know anything about the events in the Kravica region in January 1993? Do you remember Christmas, the 7th of January, 1993?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where were you then?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was working on a house for some people in Crna Rijeka in Srebrenica on that day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you working inside or outside of the house?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Inside the house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At any time did you find out that something was happening about food?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How did you find out?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sidik Memic and Safik Memic came to me and told me, Stop your work, we're going to Kravica for food.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were they fighters or civilians, those two men?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Civilians.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. And then what happened?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I stopped with my work, I went home, took what I needed, and set off towards Kravica that same evening.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know the terrain towards Kravica?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the way to Kravica, were you alone or were you in a group of people?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were a number of people with us. A single person meant nothing, only a number of people.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: A number of people. How many people is that? Many? Few?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were many people.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. And did you see any people who were coming back at the same time from Kravica or not?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did see them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what were these people doing?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Most of them were carrying food.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you speak with any of them? Were you interested in finding out what was going over there?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We asked them where we could pass through and where was the safest pass so that we could get some food.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did they mention any people that were killed or wounded or not?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. They said that there were a lot of wounded and killed and they said to be careful. They told us to be careful.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did they explain how these people were killed and where the danger was?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. They told us that the most dangerous spots were in the centre of Kravica, around the school, and the entrance from Bratunac, that that was where most of our people were killed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. And when did you arrive at Kravica?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, let's say -- I can't really tell you the exact time but it was sometime in the morning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was that the 8th of January, 1992 [as interpreted]?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how much time did you need to get there?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: In normal circumstances we needed some six or seven hours. But as it was it took us at least 12 hours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because of the shelling, the shooting from various weapons. A person had to seek cover in order to reach Kravica to get some food.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please, when you say "shelling" was this, according to what you know, if you can answer, was this Serb shelling or Muslim shelling?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was Serb shelling.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. So you came to Kravica on the 8th of January. Did you see what Kravica looked like on that day?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If anyone were to say that on the 7th of January, 1992, Kravica was burned to the ground would that be true?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please explain to the Chamber why not.

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because on the 8th when I got there there was damage to the houses from the shooting and the shelling, but as far as I could see only two houses had burned down. How they burned down, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Were you there alone when you entered Kravica?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not by myself. There were thousands of people there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you describe to the Trial Chamber what these people were doing, these thousands of people?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were getting food.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where were they getting the food from on the 8th?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the houses.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And were those houses burning at the time?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: How could they be burning? How would a person enter a burning house to get food?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And could you tell us what you found. Did you find anything in the houses?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I found 25 litres of rakija, plum brandy, and five kilogrammes of honey also.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why was rakija important to you? Could you please explain to the Trial Chamber. First of all, I would like to ask you: Do you drink alcohol?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sometimes. Rakija was precious as a substitute for any food. It was useful for me to be able to feed my family.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Actually, did you want to say that you could barter or trade that for any other food?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. For flour and other things.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you find anything else?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I found a rifle at the same place where I found the rakija.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What kind of a rifle was it?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was an automatic rifle.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Tiro, did you hand this rifle over to anyone?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was the only way for me to go in search of food more freely.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What does that mean? What did that rifle mean to you?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: It meant that I could go anywhere and it was my only salvation, the only way that I could save my life.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you remain in Kravica for a long time on the 8th?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why not?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because I found what I needed and I returned and also because of the shelling and the shooting. I wanted to save myself.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say "shelling" what exactly do you mean?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mean shelling. I also mean airplanes, intense firing, any person who thought rationally had to get out of there to save their life.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Tiro, in spite of the shelling and the shooting, were people still coming into Kravica and looking for food there?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, on a daily basis.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How was this possible at all in such a situation? Were people paying heed to the danger at all?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was important for people to either find food in order to survive or they would get killed. They would be dead in any case, either from lack of food or from a bullet or a shell.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now I would like to ask you something else. At the time when you were in Kravica, you found a rifle there. Did there come a time that you joined a unit?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: A group of armed soldiers?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Which group?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I joined the Cizmici with Ejub Golic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, out of my own free will.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, you decided that, but why did you decide to join Ejub Golic?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because I knew that man from before.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I would like to ask you this: How long did you spend in Ejub Golic's group; do you remember?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I spent a long time with Ejub Golic defending Cizmici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During the time you were in that group, did you have contacts with Mr. Ejub Golic, did you have personal contacts with him?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you have several contacts with him or not?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We were in touch on several occasions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell us, do you have any information about whether Mr. Ejub Golic Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. and that group of people around him considered anybody in Srebrenica as their commander? Was it stated that there was a command in Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was this command in Srebrenica mentioned at all to you in any way?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And now I would like to ask you another question. The entire time in 1992 until the demilitarisation in 1993, did you receive any kind of summons for mobilisation? Did anyone ever try to mobilise you?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The fact that you went to Ejub Golic's unit, was that of your own free will? Were you able to go anywhere or -- could you please explain this to the Trial Chamber?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Once I found the rifle, I could go to any unit. It doesn't -- it didn't matter whether it was Ejub Golic's group or any other group. I went to his group because he's from my municipality and Cizmici were the only ones that remained in the Bratunac municipality.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, Madam Vidovic. Yes, Ms. Sellers, are you in a position to start your cross now?

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, I'd like to start my cross.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: But I probably will end a bit earlier today. If you will give me one minute.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Please ask whatever you need. We have got ample time since we are not going to get a new witness tomorrow. The witness doesn't need a break, does he? Mr. Tiro, you don't -- can we proceed straight away with the cross-examination or do you need a break?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We can start, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Cross-examined by Ms. Sellers:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you for allowing us to start, Mr. Tiro.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: I would ask the usher to assist in moving that back.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: That's much better.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Tiro, my name is Patricia Sellers, and as I've stated earlier today I'm with the Office of the Prosecution. Now, you've just answered the questions of Madam Vidovic and right now it is the Prosecutor who will ask you some questions based upon many of the answers that you've given but also about things that are relevant to this case, meaning what happened to you during the time period of 1992 and 1993. If there is something that I'm asking that you don't understand, please indicate that to me. But there will be other times when I'm merely trying to ask a question that requires either a yes or no answer, and if you could limit yourself to that, that will assist us. But if there comes a time period when you would want to elaborate a bit, please feel free to do so. Now, can I just reconfirm some of the information, Mr. Tiro. You testified that you were born in 1961. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you have two brothers, Mehmed and Hamdija?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, are you the oldest of your -- of the three brothers in your family?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you tell us who is the older brother.

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Hamdija.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what year was Hamdija born in?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you testified that the year that Mehmed was born in is 1968. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, did all of your brothers attend school in Bjelovac like you did?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did and my older brother. Mehmed went to elementary school in Fakovici and secondary school in Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you've testified also that you served in the JNA, as many people in your area did, and that in particular you were in the brigade that was concerned with the mountains and the infantry. Could you just explain to me a bit what exactly were your services when you were in the JNA.

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I personally served in the mountain infantry, and finally at the time I served I ended up as a machine-gunner.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now -- excuse me. Someone who serves in the mountain infantry, would that person have to have knowledge of mountain trails or mountain paths or how to survive in a mountainous terrain?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And are these some of --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment. All of this or -- because you put at least three things in the same -- let's --

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you could just specify a bit more clearly for Your Honour. So we've talked about somebody having to understand -- have knowledge of mountain trails. Is this among the things, the services, or things -- skills that you learned in the JNA?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I've learned quite a lot in the JNA.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Explain to Your Honours then in terms of how to survive in a mountainous terrain or your knowledge of mountain trails what it is exactly that you learned in the JNA about that.

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Even then when I served with the JNA we went on a track sometimes up to 40 kilometres, sometimes even without food in order to be able to survive anything. No one was hoping that this war was take place, but in that way they were preparing us for any sort of future war and to survive. That's the way the then-army helped us, and later on of course we were fighting against it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you also explain to Your Honours then, you've mentioned that not only did you have to learn to survive the mountains but part of your JNA service included knowledge of artillery.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'd like to apologise to Ms. Sellers for interrupting. I would like to correct the transcript. The witness said at that time the army helped us and then it did everything in order not to help us. And it wasn't specifically said that the witness said later on we had to fight against it. Did I understand you correctly, Mr. Tiro?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right, yes. My apologies to you, Ms. Sellers.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Yes, thank you, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you explain to Your Honours not only the skills you learned concerning mountain survival but using artillery or, as you've testified, a machine-gunner within the brigade that was learning the skills related to the mountain? Did you learn how to use weapons in the mountain during your JNA service?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please explain to the Trial Chamber the skills needed for using weapons in mountainous terrains, the types of weapons, and the types of things that someone in your position learned.

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: In mountain terrains and in the positions that are set up one usually uses a machine-gun, a mortar, or a hand-held mortar. And all of the soldiers are train in that, not to use just one piece of or type of weaponry but several. And once the training is finished, and it was a rather long one, it lasted for six months, they were all qualified to man such weapons. One could learn where that type of weaponry originated from, how it functions, and how it is to be used. We couldn't leave for the mountains and take heavy artillery -- take guns with us or to have a tank because the terrain was too steep, hence we had to use paths, trails, and there is a reason and a justification for the type of weaponry used in the mountains, and it's usually what you can carry on your back.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So in the transport of weapons up mountain paths and trails, was this part of the training that you learned when you were in the JNA?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, did that training also include the possibility of using animals, such as horses, to take weapons up mountain trails or paths?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, for the more heavy weapons.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, would you tell the Trial Chamber, did you therefore have to learn how to handle horses in their transporting or assisting you to transport weapons within mountainous areas?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. In mountain units, horses had to undergo training as well as soldiers. And they were quite a help to the soldiers, otherwise all the weaponry had to be carried on the soldier's back, including the mountain devices for the machine-guns and so on and so forth. That's why we used the horses; otherwise the lighter weapons could be carried on our backs.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So would you agree that horses during a time of war were a valuable commodity or means of transporting weapons?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It was worthier, or rather more valuable than an ordinary soldier or any soldier for that matter.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, did your brothers also do JNA service as they were growing up close to the time period that you did your JNA service?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I served the military in 1980 and my brother in 1981, which was somewhat late for his age. The younger brother did his service in 1986.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So if I understand your testimony, that means that Hamdija did his service in 1981. Is that correct, Mr. Tiro?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, what type of service did he do in the JNA?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was in the communications centre.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And could you tell the Trial Chamber what types of skills, if you know, was he expected to learn by being a member of the communications centre or in the communications centre training.

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't explain to the Chamber his service. I only know that his service was with the communications centre. I wasn't familiar with that and I can't explain anything pertaining to his service.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just briefly coming back to your service within the mountain brigade, did you have to, as related to fighting on a mountain terrain, deal with the issue of communications also?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. As an ordinary soldier, these were regular duties.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did that mean that you would learn how to communicate from one mountainous terrain to another location or possibly another mountainous terrain?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course. One wouldn't be a good soldier without having learned those activities.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I agree. And a good soldier -- well, maybe you could tell us, how would a good soldier communicate under those types of conditions? And I'm referring to conditions of being in the infantry, the mountainous Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. infantry, possibly during battle.

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the JNA we were taught, because such was the command, one couldn't disobey an officer, just do what you were told and you had to learn that. There was no one to defend a soldier at that time if he disobeyed or said anything to an officer; he could only be sent to prison.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Tiro. We'll come back to that, but I wanted to ask you and maybe you didn't understand my question. When I'm speaking about communications I'm speaking about Motorolas or hand-held radios or RUP-12s. Did you know or have to learn about those means of communication while you did your JNA service?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I wasn't forced to learn that. Just those soldiers who were with the command post, and I was a regular soldier.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you able to learn anything about couriers or the carrying of messages in between units or groups while you were in your JNA service, that form of communication?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. The couriers were used for that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So were the couriers different and distinguished from members of a unit or infantry group that were concerned with mountainous artillery? Were the couriers a different group of soldiers?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Those were usually couriers attached to officers and they didn't have anything to do with heavy weaponry.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, I want to ask you one or two other questions about your JNA service, and the first is: Geographically where did you serve, in what region of the former Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I served in Pljevlja in Montenegro.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the other question I'd like to ask is that after you came out of the JNA in 1980, did you ever use some of the skills, particularly just the skills of going in and out of the mountains near your home or the region where you lived, that you had learned in the JNA?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I didn't have the time for that because I worked more than was necessary.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever climb mountain trails during that time period or possibly go to other hamlets or locations using back woods or back trails?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Tiro, in June 1992 you've been able to testify at the Tribunal that there was increasing tension between Muslims and Serbs and that there were conflicts in Bradjevina and Rakovici. I would like to ask you: Prior to those conflicts what were your brothers, Hamdija and Mehmed, doing in terms of the tension?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: My brother Mehmed was with me. Hamdija was in Kosovo in a mine called Kisnica there. He worked there. And I have evidence that he left on the 6th of January of 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when did he join you?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Never. I haven't seen him until this day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you have testified that during the month of June that you were not engaged in any way in any type of military formation. My question to you is that did you participate in the village guards?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't actively participate in a village guard because I had no arms. Had I had a rifle I would have participated.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Tiro, isn't it possible that you could bring information about what was happening in your area to members who were armed, that it wasn't necessary to have an arm to participate in the village guard?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: To what units should I communicate such information because there were no units in my surroundings, in the Muslim villages? There couldn't be a unit without a rifle.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Tiro, I'm not referring to units. I'm referring to villagers who might have armed themselves to protect their homes.

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I explained already. There was no point in transferring information to the two people who had rifles in order for them to try and save two or 300 houses.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Tiro, isn't it a fact that you did go around and you did communicate information during that time period? You spoke to various people, so you've testified, including Bosnian Serbs, as to the different, from your testimony, build-up of Serb military. Isn't it true that you did communicate information to people?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Objection, Your Honour. The witness never said that he transferred information. Rather, as far as I understood it, he received information.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: He's being asked whether he transferred -- he passed on information.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: This is what he's being asked. There's no question in asking him again to repeat that he received information. What he's being asked is whether he passed on that information to others. As I understand --

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: If I misunderstand you, then please correct me.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: No, this is precisely --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There was no one for me to pass such information to. The same way that such information reached other people, it was the way that I would receive them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Tiro, how would you receive your information?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: As part of my evidence here, it comes from me personally seeing things and experiencing them.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Objection, Your Honour. When he says "I received information" we should be very specific as to the sort of information, otherwise we confuse the witness. He spoke about the entire spectrum of information here.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm going to specify this in the next question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. I think the objection is quite pertinent and I would suggest that you do, Ms. Sellers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Tiro, I just want to take you back to your testimony about the school in Ruljevici. Do you remember your testimony there, concerning the school?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you testified that you were at the house of a Serb acquaintance, and you were able to observe what appeared to be men that you recognised at the school in camouflage uniforms and with weapons. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not in the house. I was in the field of this person called Prokic, Zivko. And it was 20 metres away across the river and I stood in the field and I was observing the school and the people.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. One moment. I saw you trying to stand up, Ms. Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I wanted to raise an objection. The Prosecutor asked the witness: "You were in the house?" And the witness said that he was in the field. That was that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That's --

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I do stand corrected. I did mean to say you were at the home of and I didn't mean to be physically in the house. I understand quite well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yeah, but that's superseded now. I think that's clear enough.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Tiro, that you were standing behind a tree, if I understand correctly?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And as you stated, you were about 20 metres away, and at that distance there was a small stream or river in between the home of your friend and the school. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Between the school and the field.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, could you hear the conversation of the men that were gathered at the school?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I could overhear the conversation if they spoke more loudly at times, but when they exchanged words between themselves I couldn't hear it from the river.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And as a matter of fact, what you could hear was when one of the men refused to take a weapon, refused to carry a weapon that was given him. Isn't that correct, Mr. Tiro?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that's because he shouted. He said something in a voice that was louder than normal conversation. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The other conversation was not at the volume of someone shouting. That's what I presume. That's correct, isn't it, Mr. Tiro?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, when you saw this event at the school, did that frighten you?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: It frightened me a lot and I was sorry to have been there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And prior to coming there you had no knowledge that these types of arrangements were taking place at the school. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And if I understand correctly, your friend didn't want you to stay too long. There came a period when he asked you to please leave because it might not be safe. Isn't that correct, Mr. Tiro?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then did you leave his house or leave the area in front of his house?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I left immediately and I couldn't go on my own but, rather, he escorted me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, when you got back to the area near your home, Gornja Orlica, did you then not tell anyone what you had seen?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I told the people of my village, in order for them to be safer in a way, so that they wouldn't be caught by surprise.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Understandable. Who did you tell, Mr. Tiro?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Who else but the people from the 18 villages that were in my village. I couldn't go to other villages to tell people.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you communicated the information to them because you wanted to tell them of a possible danger. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Because the entire village was actually one family.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you then discuss with any of the villagers possible means for protection or what they should do if the danger were to manifest itself?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I was telling them about the possibility of fleeing into the woods, but otherwise we couldn't protect ourselves. We had no arms.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Tiro, let me just ask you: In terms of the two people who had arms in our village, would you please tell the Trial Chamber what their names were.

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not in my hamlet but in the village of Zapolje, that's where the two people with rifles were. But there were no arms in my hamlet of Krnolica [phoen].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I stand corrected. Please tell me the names of the two people in Zapolje then.

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Cazim Sinanovic was an active policeman, and Seval Husic, a Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. reserve policeman.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And these were policemen attached to what police station?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And would you tell the Trial Chamber the weapons that they had -- yes?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Seval Husic had a semi-automatic rifle and Cazim Sinanovic an automatic one.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Tiro, were any of the members, and here I'll specifically refer to the male members, in your village and the surrounding villages members of the TO forces or reserve TO before 1992 or just up until 1992?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you a member of the reserved TO forces?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you or any of those other men in this area have any weapons for hunting?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nobody in my village. In Tegare about ten people did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in the villages that were surrounding Tegare that you have mentioned, are you -- is your testimony to the Trial Chamber that there were no armed men in the Muslim villages?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Just the two in Zapolje. As concerns Gornja Orlica, my hamlet, as well as Donja Orlica, the 30 houses, there were no arms there.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The question was a confusing one and the witness misunderstood. When he said the villages surrounding his, then he should say Muslim villages, Serb villages, or rather what villages are in question because the witness doesn't understand the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I don't see how the witness could have misunderstood the question because we've been talking about Muslims. So I would imagine what Ms. Sellers has asked the witness throughout is she wants to establish whether Muslims in the area were armed or not. So that's what the witness ought to address.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can we just clarify that. Is that what you responded to, Mr. Tiro, concerning whether the Muslim men had arms in relationship to the questions I've just asked you?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And if we want to be more precise, in the Muslim villages.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: In the Muslim villages, yes, the men in those villages.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Or hamlets or whatever because I don't know what they --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I replied just those ten hunting rifles there and two in Zapolje. Around me in the Muslim villages, around me there were no more rifles than that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Tiro --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment. Rifles or -- these are rifles or shotguns or what? Because now we are using the word "rifles" and before we were using "hunting."

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But if I understand your testimony correctly - and, Mr. Tiro, please tell me if it's not correct - are you referring to rifles in terms of the men in Tegare and then there were semi-automatic weapons in terms of the two other men in Zapolje. Is that correct, Mr. Tiro?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: A hunter did not take an automatic rifle when he went hunting, so I'm thinking of a hunting rifle, a shotgun.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Is that clear?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: A shotgun is not a rifle. I mean, it's -- I at least -- from what I have learned they have never meant the same.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Well, we're --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You can have hunting rifles.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: A shotgun is a shotgun and a rifle is a rifle.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: We're going to ask Mr. Tiro, who has done his JNA service, to enlighten us a bit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: A rifle is a rifle because of the rifling inside the barrel --

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: The mechanism --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: No, the rifle, it's a grooving that they do, while a shotgun is something completely different. The process of firing a rifle, a bullet from a rifle is completely different from the process of firing a cartridge from a shotgun.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: I stand educated, Your Honours. Let me just check with Mr. Tiro.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Tiro, are we talking about rifles, the two rifles in Tegare and or are we talking about shotguns, or a combination of both?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is a Sacmarica rifle. It's different. It's not hard ammunition. You have buck shot and that rifle can kill as well, except this one has more killing range. It's broader, whereas the combat ammunition goes in only one direction.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Exactly. A shotgun spreads out and it spreads out according to the size of the pellets that are contained, unless it's an elephant shotgun where you have got one cartridge shooting one big elephant.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So, Mr. Tiro, if I understand correctly with the weapons that you have just described, these weapons can be used both for hunting and in terms of other forms of killing. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was legally issued not to kill people but to go rabbit hunting or to hunt other game. It wasn't for killing. It was something that was legally owned. A person would receive a license for it. Not everybody could be issued with such a rifle.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, I'd like to know: How did you know that there were ten of these rifles in Tegare? How did you receive that information?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's a village right next to my village. It's close by. And I knew people who would pass by on their way to go hunting by my house, I knew these people.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And isn't it information that in April 1992 through June 1992 became fairly important to know how many weapons or arms that the Muslim population in this region had? You would agree with that, wouldn't you?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The Serbs were already asking about that and they were ordering them to hand over these hunting rifles. But some people actually just went to the woods and they didn't give their rifles in.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You're talking about people other than the 12 people that we've identified so far, or are you talking about those 12 owners of weapons?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: About those people, those people.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay, Mr. Tiro, I would like to ask you a couple of questions concerning the beginning of July 1992. And there came a time, you've testified, that you and members of your family went to Srebrenica. That was after the 4th of July, I think around the 6th of July, 1992. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, did you walk to Srebrenica with your family or were you also with other people going in that direction?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: We didn't have any means of transportation. We walked.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And if I remember your testimony correctly, you walked through a dense wood or woods before coming to Srebrenica. Correct?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, were you leading your family or you and your brothers leading your family through the terrain, including the woods, to get to Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not all of my brothers. One of my brothers and also my brother-in-law. We took our family to Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you for the correction. Were you therefore leading them through this terrain, including the dense woods?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And am I to understand that you knew about the woods or a bit of this terrain before you led them through or you didn't know anything about how to arrive in Srebrenica in that manner?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wasn't there before. However, necessity makes one learn about everything or necessity requires that a person gets acquainted with everything.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And at this point in time when necessity required your becoming acquainted with this physical terrain, can I assume that you were able to draw on some of the skills that you learned in your JNA service?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. You don't need skills there. There's just fear and goodwill needed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I agree with that, but what about in terms of walking through the woods? Wasn't it your testimony that there were potentially or possibly Serb forces in Spat that you had to go around -- I believe it was Skenderovici to come behind Srebrenica in the woods?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't even pass through Skenderovici. And it's not only Spat. Pribicevac is also there. It's completely around Skenderovici. So I went behind Skenderovici and through the woods and behind Pribicevac through the woods in order to get my family to Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. And also in order to avoid being engaged by any hostile fire. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, there's nothing to respond with. I didn't have ammunition. I mean, I could only get killed. I had to pass in order to avoid them so that myself and my family wouldn't get killed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One thing, Ms. Sellers, that has been on my mind since -- even since the examination-in-chief started: If you were not familiar with that particular terrain and area, how would you find your way? How would you know exactly which -- which trail to follow, which direction to go? Were you carrying a map, a survey map, for example?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I didn't have a map. I had an idea more or less how to get to Zeleni Jadar and to Srebrenica, which road to take. So it's the Bratunac and Srebrenica municipality. A person couldn't really get lost there. I knew or we knew where the Serb villages were.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Yes, Ms. Sellers. Sorry to have interrupted.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: That's fine.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Tiro, back to going towards Srebrenica, did you always stay on the road except for the one time that you entered the woods or did you go inside and to the forest alongside of the woods? Could you make that a bit clearer for us.

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: From Mocevici to below Skenderovici, because Skenderovici is in the hills. We -- so we took the road. Below Skenderovici we turned into the woods and went through the woods all the way to Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So am I to understand that between Gornja Orlica just to before you get to Skenderovici that you were able to take the roads in order to walk in the direction of Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it's not clear to me how -- from Orlica. That question is Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. not clear.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Let me rephrase it then. You and your family left from Gornja Orlica. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: From Gornja Orlica on the 12th of May.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I'm talking about the 6th of July, when you were going towards Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 6th of July I set out from Mocevici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think --

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you explain describe the part of your journey - and thank you for that correction - of when you were on the road or when you had to leave the road and go into a different area, a wooded area, from Mocevici on the way to Srebrenica, please.

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Below Dimnici, perhaps about a kilometre away from there. I could reach that part by road already from Dimnici. Below Dimnici behind -- after Pribicevac we went through the woods all the way to Srebrenica because you didn't dare go out into the road.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, the part of the road that you were able to travel on, was that part of the road being shelled or did you see any weapons or hear any -- or were you shot at during that part?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It was coming from Pribicevci and from Bezani also, but I was never in Bezani. This is right off from Dimnici and Storeska from a hill. That's why we had to move during the night to cover that part of the road.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you were able to take the road down in night-time in the cover of dark?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. And then you entered into the woods. Now, when you went into the woods between -- below Skenderovici up to Srebrenica, did you see other people in the woods?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There was a group of people there, those who were able to walk. The elderly were not able to join them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And were you following a path in the woods or were you just going through the woods where there was no indication or trails, paths, or roads of any degree?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, there were no paths. It was just the forest.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, when you arrive in Srebrenica, you've testified that you were able to find housing in Petrici, if I'm pronouncing that correctly, a section of the city?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't say Petrici. I said when we came down into Srebrenica we came -- we reached Srebrenica at Petrici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where did you find your lodging at, sir?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I passed through the centre of Srebrenica and I found accommodation near the bus station.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How did you find accommodation? Did you ask a person? Did anyone inform you where it would be?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I asked a certain Amir Murathodzic and he told me, Here, you can move into this house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, the house that you moved into I'm assuming it was an empty house, that there was no one living in it at that moment?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Nobody was living there for a while.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there a possibility of staying in any other accommodation or other house or was this the only one that was indicated to you?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't need to look at anything else. It was important to me just to move somewhere. I wasn't looking for a large space or anything. I had what I needed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You testified that there were other relatives that joined you, lived with you, in that house at a later date. Would you please remind me, what date did the other relatives join you?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: After 15 or 20 days.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, the house you moved into, you say that the man -- I'm just trying to remember his name. He said that you could move in. Did he indicate that you had to move into this house or there was no other accommodation or was this just a helpful suggestion?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just to help me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, were there other people coming into Srebrenica at that time that were having houses indicated to them where they might move in?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. People were arriving but later there was no need for anyone to tell them where they could move into.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was that because they chose to move into certain houses on their own, Mr. Tiro?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: The authority was not functioning any longer. There were empty houses. Everybody moved in in order to get their family inside so that they wouldn't be left outside, and there was nobody who could prevent them from doing that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you stated that other members of your family joined you about 15 or 20 days later. Did you invite them to stay with you or did another person indicate that they should stay with you?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I invited them. I wanted to shelter the children.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And, Mr. Tiro, to your knowledge, was there any requisitioning of household goods or materials from any of the apartments or houses in Srebrenica that no longer had their owners, that were abandoned?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, because there was nothing to be built. Those who stayed had their own accommodation, their own things. I think that even in 1995 those things remained in Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I don't know, there may have been a misinterpretation of the word "requisitioning." That's what I suspect. At the time that Ms. Sellers is directing your attention to, she is suggesting that there must have been some houses which were vacant. The question is whether they were being sequestered, taken possession of, and made available to those who needed accommodation. This is the question that I understand Ms. Sellers as having put to you, but I don't know whether it was translated -- yes, Madam Vidovic, if I am wrong please do correct me.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I would kindly ask that the word be explained to the witness, the word "requisition" because I think the witness who has only completed eight years of elementary school can understand [as interpreted] this word.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Tiro, let me explain very briefly. In the concept of social housing there is -- and especially in times of emergency, vacant houses are taken possession of by the authorities, usually by the housing department or whatever, social housing department, and made available to those who do not have anywhere to live and who need accommodation. Ms. Sellers is asking you whether at the time that you arrived in Srebrenica there was such a system, however loose it may be, that was in operation. In other words, would someone arrive in Srebrenica homeless, without having a place where to go to and someone would come forward and say, We have made available this accommodation or this house or this apartment for those who are homeless? Was there anything of this sort occurring at the time? Are you happy with the explanation that I have given because I don't think I can explain it more than that. I changed the word "requisitioning" to "sequester," thinking that it may be probably translated better, but I don't know if I have made myself clear to Mr. Tiro. Have you understood me, Mr. Tiro?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes, Your Honour. There was nobody representing the authorities at that time, and there was no authority at all when I came to Srebrenica so that nobody could mobilise these facilities. The people moved in on their own to places that were already empty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. If you want to proceed on this matter you are free to do so because I intervened more or less, and I don't want you to think that I was cutting you off.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: No. I just have a couple more questions concerning this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I would like to know. You said that you -- you testified that you spoke to Amir Murakovic?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Murathodzic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know him prior to coming to Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't know him. I only got to know him then and there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And is it your testimony that you met him when you arrived and he offered or suggested that you move into that housing, those accommodations?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I asked him -- I met him. I didn't know him, and I asked him if there was any space anywhere where I could put my family. He looked at my sister's two children and he said, Well, there's this house right here. It's not much but you can move in for a time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And, Mr. Tiro, if I understand correctly, then the house you moved into was near the centre of town?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it wasn't near the centre of town. It was a bit -- it was near the bus station.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And you met Mr. Murakovic - I'm sorry for my mispronunciation - near the centre of town. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: He also had a house that was right across the street from the bus station.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, Mr. Tiro --

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: I have a couple more questions, Your Honour, before we go to the break.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Tiro, when your extended family, when your other family came 15 or 18 days later, did you have to or were you able to gather any more blankets, bedding, or things that they might use while in the accommodation?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. They were people there from Srebrenica who helped us and gave us bedding and bedcovers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, were these people who were acting individually? Were these people that were acting as a community group, or were these people with any other type of configuration?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: These were things that we got from people of good will. There was no organisation in this at all.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Tiro, you've testified that you've basically were born, raised, in this geographical area of the Srebrenica municipality near to Bratunac. Had you ever been to Srebrenica before this time period, July 6th, 1992?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I wasn't born in the geographical area of the Srebrenica municipality. I was born in the Bratunac municipality area.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think it's --

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: I understand his confusion. Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Had you ever been to the town of Srebrenica before this, before July 6th, 7th, 1992?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the 1980s I went to Srebrenica on one occasion, but it wasn't on my way. I didn't pass through there whenever I went anywhere. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And can I also ask you: Were you aware when you came towards Srebrenica, and maybe one of your reasons for going there, is that the town was still considered a safer town or a safe town for the Muslim inhabitants of Srebrenica municipality or adjacent Bratunac municipality?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: We didn't know but we decided to come to Srebrenica. Only later when we arrived we saw that there were a lot of people there, so whatever happened to them would happen to us. But there was never any talk about going to Bratunac from the beginning of the war.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So if I can understand clearly, it's your testimony that you went to Srebrenica without knowing that Srebrenica had become -- the city of Srebrenica had become a type of safe place or safer place for Muslims? You didn't have that information?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would like to stop my questions right here, and I'm going to consult with my co-counsels to see whether I'll continue this afternoon's -- for our next session or just re-commence tomorrow morning, if you don't mind.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Do you need to -- do you want to consult now?

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Could I please do that now?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, I think it would be better.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think we will continue and I will say that possibly the next session just will not take the full 45 minutes or it might. Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So we'll have a 30-minute break and we'll restart at 1.00. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Sellers, please go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Tiro, are you fine to continue?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. I'd like to go back to the topic that we were discussing and it was about how you were living in Srebrenica. My next question, Mr. Tiro, is just to confirm that you're unaware of any authorities that existed in Srebrenica from July 1992 until what time period?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Allegedly, the authorities never existed or were never recognised even in that period of 1995. There was no authority over so many people. I could have placed myself in a position of authority but no one would follow. And that didn't include just one municipality but several.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So, Mr. Tiro, if I understand correctly, when you're speaking about the authorities or the lack of authorities in Srebrenica between 1992 up until 1995, you're speaking in broad generalities comparing Srebrenica and other municipalities like Bratunac. Is that what I'm understanding?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes. The municipality of Bratunac, a part of the Visegrad municipality, Han Pijesak, Vlasenica, Zvornik, all of the people were there in Srebrenica, and there was no respect for authority. People were fighting over food. The authorities would be of no help. If one appointed oneself, no one obeyed. We were not interested in any sort of authority, we were interested in survival only.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Then let me ask you some specific questions. Would it be your testimony that in 1992 in Srebrenica town when you arrived there that you were unaware of any formation called a War Presidency or municipal government?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was there but I wasn't interested.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now I understand more precisely. Can I ask you the same question: Were you aware of any civilian police authorities?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And we've touched on it briefly, but were you aware of any types of housing authorities?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was impossible for any body of authority to exist and people, as they came, tried to find their own accommodation. And there was no such authority regarding houses, but there were no bans either. People who were living there would allow people to move in to use a part of their house in order for them to survive.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Let me continue a bit in this vein of questioning. Were you aware of any military police authorities?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And were you aware of any military authorities located in the town of Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No such organs were not in place, the military ones.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Let me go back to what we've -- what you've testified about it in terms of the War Presidency and I believe that you said that -- you admitted that it might have existed, that you just were not interested in it. Would you please tell the Trial Chamber when you understood me to say "War Presidency" what that meant to you. Describe what a War Presidency is for you.

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: A War Presidency, I guess that pertained to the municipality or the building there. But I had no opportunity and I didn't want to go to the building of the municipality and what people were doing there. I was busy with my own life.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. You're referring to a physical building in the town of Srebrenica, Mr. Tiro, when you're talking about municipality?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. So if I were to ask you whether you knew who was the president of the War Presidency, could I assume that you wouldn't know that person's name?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I didn't know people in Srebrenica. I wasn't interested in finding out who was who or to learn their names.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you do not know Hajrudin Avdic?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you testified that you were unaware of any types of civilian police forces. I'd like to ask you have you ever heard of the name Becir Bogilovic?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you aware that there was a SUP building, a building where the police had been housed, prior to the war in Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw that building in passing and I saw that some people lived in that house, in that building.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever hear people speaking about any police activities going on in that building, Mr. Tiro?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: People were not talking about it. And had there been any police, I must have seen it and I suppose they would wear police insignia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Tiro, if I understand correctly that prior to the war that you were in the building trade, that you assisted in the construction of buildings. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What types of construction projects were you involved in?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Anything that a construction worker could do or build.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would that include houses, public buildings, commercial buildings?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And also, if I remember your testimony correctly, that you received training in this field and it appears that you practiced this profession for a number of years prior to the war, at least ten years. Is that correct, Mr. Tiro?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, did you work for someone else or did you have your own construction firm?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I worked for other people.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: He gave us this information yesterday.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, he gave us the name of a company. I'm not quite certain what was his relationship.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: No, he said that he worked with this company, and then upon another question from Ms. Vidovic he also acknowledged that from a certain time, 1988 if I remember well, he had his own company.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Yes. Okay. Fine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But please go ahead because I may be mistaken.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Tiro, could you just briefly explain that to us, in terms of your years in your profession, your career, your working status as a worker or as an owner.

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was a worker in a company. I wasn't an owner. As of 1988 I started working by myself with a smaller group of people, not only in our immediate area but all over former Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you would travel certainly around the municipality of Bratunac and adjoining municipalities as well as the entire former Yugoslavia. Is that what I'm to understand by your testimony?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in -- and in undertaking the work, whether it be as the worker or as the owner in your smaller firm, would you at times be asked to do repair work, to repair structures as well as building structures?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I was employed with the company, this is what I was doing, repairing buildings. I also constructed them. Later on when I left the company, I mainly worked on family houses.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And with your work on family houses, would that include putting in windows, putting in doors, walls, all types of structures that are nascent to a house in which people live?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Tiro, you testified that when you came to Srebrenica that there was a time period when you were also engaged in building or construction work. Would you just explain to the Trial Chamber what time period are we talking about and what type of construction work were you doing in Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Preparing houses, and when the Swedish project was underway in Srebrenica, then I worked with the people from Sweden in Zeleni Jadar in setting up building projects.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, between July 1992, when you arrived, up until December 1992, were you engaged in some construction work in Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was only helping to those who needed some repair of a, say, a room for them to be accommodated somewhere to survive.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, just for a point of information, in your assisting or helping of others, was this something that you did individually, voluntarily, or is this something you did in an organised -- a more organised fashion, possibly with other people who also knew how to -- who had that trade?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. It was voluntarily. I went by myself and if somebody wanted to join in, that was all right. But if one didn't want to there was no one to force him. But people were helping each other because there was no other way. It's better to help someone than to leave his family outdoors.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I certainly agree. And I'm wondering, did you offer your services to any type of authority that might be able to tell you which people or where the construction should take place or where the materials could be gathered for construction?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. And I wasn't familiar with any such organisation or authority Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. that would have construction material. When I would see someone working, I would approach and join in.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever have people give you material that came from houses in the surroundings of Srebrenica or from towns outside of Srebrenica? Building material, I mean.

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: If someone had anything, they gave; if not, then it had to be gotten from somewhere. That's as far as I know. But the people who were initiating these repairs, but as to how they went about it I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you yourself ever seek building materials outside of the town of Srebrenica that you could bring back to Srebrenica to construct with?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Personally, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know people who did do that?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO [Resumed]
